key_insight: A planner-executor multimodal AI system can both answer lung cancer screening CT questions and appropriately defer out-of-scope questions to a doctor.
clinical_relevance: If validated in real-world workflows, this could improve patient understanding of screening results and support follow-up adherence while preserving clinician oversight.
method: Used 116 lung cancer screening CT reports and images from a tertiary academic hospital.
Generated 699 simulated patient questions, split into answerable and defer-to-doctor categories.
Evaluated tool-calling, self-regulation, and clinical quality with LLM judges and four physicians.
evidence_signal: Performance was strong: tool-calling accuracy was 93.1% and self-regulation accuracy was 92.6%, with high physician-rated clinical accuracy and understandability scores.
watch_item: Results come from retrospective data and simulated questions, so real-world patient use, safety, and workflow impact still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Planner-Executor Style Multimodal Agentic System to Answer Patient Questions in Lung Cancer Screening CT
